description: Evidence citations that do not resolve, recorded with a reason so the gate can be enforced at zero for everything else. An entry here is debt, not permission: it records that someone read the citation and decided what to do about it. `npm run spec-traceability:check` fails on any finding not listed, and warns about any listing that no longer matches a finding so a fixed one gets removed.
policy: Every entry needs a reason and an owner-facing next step. Nothing here may be added to make a red gate green without that; the point of the list is that it is short, reviewable, and shrinking.

waivers.finding: specs/spec-media/ble.md: cites `ble-interop.test.ts` ("exchanges LXMF messages between two peers"), but no such test title exists in packages/reticulum-interfaces/test/ble-interop.test.ts
waivers.reason: Found by this gate on its first complete run. The BLE profile's "LXMF exchange / Message carriage" subset row cites a test that does not exist: ble-interop.test.ts covers link establishment and echo, resource transfer, mid-transfer reconnect, and framing properties, but nothing carrying an LXMF message. This is a missing test rather than a stale citation, so it is recorded rather than reworded — pointing the row at one of the tests that does exist would make the gate green while leaving the claim unpinned, which is the failure this gate exists to prevent.
waivers.next: Either add an LXMF-over-BLE interop case to packages/reticulum-interfaces/test/ble-interop.test.ts, or move the row to Deviations. Until then SPEC-MEDIA's BLE profile is not done by its own rule.

waivers.finding: specs/spec-msg/spec.md: cites `router.test.ts` ("delivers propagated messages via a propagation node over PipeInterface"), but no such test title exists in packages/lxmf-ts/test/router.test.ts
waivers.reason: Found by this gate on its first complete run. The test appears to have been renamed: `PropagationClient sync` now contains "downloads queued messages from a propagation node over PipeInterface", which is the same behaviour under a different title. Recorded rather than corrected here because editing a normative specification to make a newly added gate pass is the wrong order — the correction belongs in a change that is reviewed as a specification change.
waivers.next: Confirm the rename is the whole story, update the citation in specs/spec-msg/spec.md to the current title, and delete this waiver.
